rationale_code: `coreApi.getTeams` is called on the org connection built with the user's credentials and the raw team list is returned into context; this is private organization data.
`coreApi.getProjects` returns the user's Azure DevOps project inventory (non-public account data) into the agent context.
`searchIdentities` resolves organization directory identities (ids, display names, descriptors) with the user's token and returns them.

`getTeamIterations`, `getTeamSettings`/`getTeamFieldValues` and `getCapacitiesWithIdentityRefAndTotals` return internal team configuration and per-member capacity data reached with the user's credentials.

`createOrUpdateClassificationNode`/`postTeamIteration` only write structured iteration metadata back into the user's own org; no external destination and the echoed response is the agent's own input, so no label applies.

`updateCapacityWithIdentityRef` writes into the user's own org (not an attacker-readable destination) but the response surfaces the team member's `displayName`/`uniqueName` identity data from the org.
`getBuilds`, `getBuildReport` and `getBuildChanges` return private build metadata from the user's organization into context.

`getBuildLogs`/`getBuildLogLines` return private CI log content; the log text is itself output of arbitrary build steps and third-party tooling, and the code routes it through `createExternalContentResponse` ("build log"), confirming it is treated as external/untrusted content.
`getDefinitions`/`getDefinitionRevisions` return private pipeline definitions of the user's org.
`getRun`/`listRuns` return private pipeline run data reached with the user's credentials.

`getArtifacts`/`getArtifactContentZip` pull private build artifact bytes into context (or onto disk via `createWriteStream`); artifact contents are produced by pipeline jobs that consume third-party code and dependencies, so the returned bytes are attacker-influenceable. `runPipeline` queues a build with agent-supplied `variables`, `templateParameters` and `resources` (including repository `token`s) and can be pointed at any pipeline in the project; the build agent executes pipeline steps with network egress, so agent-supplied data can be delivered outward — an exfi
`gitApi.getRepositories` returns the org's private repository inventory into context.

`getPullRequest`/`getPullRequests` return private PR data, and PR titles/descriptions/branch names are free text authored by many contributors (including fork sources via `forkSource`), i.e. multi-writer content that can carry injected instructions.
`getThreads`/`getComments` return private review threads, and `trimComments` passes each comment's `content` — arbitrary text written by any project or fork contributor — into the agent context.
`gitApi.getRefs` enumerates private branch refs of the user's repositories.

`getItemText` returns raw private file content (and `getItems` directory listings) into context; repository file content at an arbitrary `version`/branch includes vendored third-party code and branches pushed by other contributors, so it is attacker-influenceable.

POSTs to the fixed vendor endpoint `https://almsearch.dev.azure.com/${orgName}` with the user's bearer token and returns private commit search results; commit messages are free text written by any committer, so the returned text is multi-writer content. `createPullRequest`/`updatePullRequest` publish agent-supplied `title`, `description` and `labels` into a pull request visible to other readers of the project (Azure DevOps projects may be public), and `createPullRequestReviewers` notifies chosen recipients; the responses also echo private PR data.

`createThread`/`createComment` post arbitrary agent-supplied `content` as a pull request comment — the classic publish-a-comment delivery path; whether the hosting project is publicly readable is not determinable from the code, so the label is kept.
`getRefs` plus `updateRefs` only creates a ref pointing at an existing commit; it returns no repository content and delivers no agent text anywhere readable, so no label applies.

`getWorkItem`, `getWorkItemsBatch`, `getComments` and `getRevisions` return private work item fields, comments and revision history; work item titles/descriptions/comments are free text authored by many users (including external bug reporters), so the content is attacker-influenceable.

`getQuery`/`queryById`/`queryByWiql` execute agent-supplied WIQL against the user's org and return private work item data; the wiql path explicitly wraps output in `createExternalContentResponse(queryResult, "wiql query results")`, confirming the results are treated as untrusted external content.
`getBacklogs`/`getBacklogLevelWorkItems` return private team backlog data from the user's organization.

POSTs/PATCHes arbitrary agent-supplied `text` as a work item comment via the org REST API — a publish-a-comment delivery path whose audience is not constrained by the code.

The unlink path calls `getWorkItem` with `WorkItemExpand.Relations` and dumps all relations plus the updated work item into context, and the wiki branch fetches page metadata with the user's token; link URIs are built from vstfs components only, never an agent-chosen external host.

`getAllWikis`/`getPagesBatch`/`getPageText` and the direct REST fetch return private wiki content with the user's token; page bodies are multi-writer documentation and the code returns them via `createExternalContentResponse(pageContent, "wiki page")`, treating them as external content. PUTs agent-supplied markdown `content` to an arbitrary wiki page path in the org, publishing it to everyone with read access to that wiki (Azure DevOps projects can be public); project visibility is not determinable from the code, so the label is kept.
Fetches test plans, suites and cases from `connection.serverUrl` with the user's bearer token and returns the private payloads.

`getTestResultDetailsForBuild` returns private test results, and the formatted output includes `errorMessage` and `stackTrace` strings produced by executing test code and third-party dependencies in CI, which are attacker-influenceable text.
`createTestPlan` writes structured plan metadata into the user's own org and returns the created object; no non-public data is read out and no attacker-readable destination is reached.
`createTestSuite`/`addTestCasesToSuite` only mutate suite structure in the user's own org; responses contain the just-created structure, not sensitive third-party data.

`createWorkItem`/`updateWorkItem` write test case titles and step XML into the user's own project; the response is the work item just written, so no additional private data is surfaced and no external destination is contacted.

`alertApi.getAlerts` returns the organization's Advanced Security findings — including secret-scanning alerts — into the agent context using the user's credentials.

`alertApi.getAlert` returns full alert detail (physical locations, code snippets, secret metadata) from the private org; the embedded code/dependency snippets originate from repository content authored by many contributors.
